questions.q: Which tribes formed the Iroquois League?
questions.explain: The Iroquois League, also called the Great League of Peace, was in the Northeast.

questions.q: There was a single Native American culture before the arrival of Europeans.
questions.explain: Tribes had different languages, political organizations, religions and ways of life.

questions.q: What does 'matrilineal' mean?
choices: Family descent is traced through the mother
The chief is always a woman
questions.explain: Some Native American societies were matrilineal.

questions.q: Which argument did Spain and Portugal use to justify colonization?
choices: Native peoples had to be converted to Christianity
Native Americans did not own the land
questions.explain: Other European countries claimed that Native Americans did not really own the land.

questions.q: Christopher Columbus reached the Bahamas on October 12, ___.
questions.explain: The date traditionally associated with his arrival.

questions.q: Where does the name 'America' come from?
questions.explain: Vespucci explored the coast of South America between 1499 and 1502.

questions.q: Who conquered the Aztec Empire in 1519?
questions.explain: Pizarro conquered the Inca Kingdom in the 1530s.

questions.q: Which disease especially devastated Native populations?
questions.explain: Epidemics, especially smallpox, plus military technology helped the conquest.

questions.q: New Amsterdam became New York in…
questions.explain: It came under English control in 1664.

questions.q: Which was the first permanent English colony, founded in 1607?
questions.explain: Roanoke (1585–1587) was unsuccessful.

questions.q: In which year did the Pilgrim Fathers arrive on the Mayflower?
questions.explain: They founded Plymouth.

questions.q: What was the last of the 13 colonies (1732)?
questions.explain: The colonies developed between 1607 and 1732.

questions.q: Massachusetts belongs to which group of colonies?
questions.explain: New England: Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, New Hampshire.

questions.q: What was 'benign neglect'?
choices: Limited British control over the colonies
questions.explain: At first Britain exercised relatively limited control. This changed after 1763.

questions.q: What did the Proclamation of 1763 do?
choices: It forbade settlers to move west beyond a boundary
questions.explain: Colonists felt Britain was blocking their westward expansion.

questions.q: No taxation without ___.
questions.explain: The colonists had no representatives in the British Parliament.

questions.q: The Stamp Act (1765) taxed…
questions.explain: It increased taxation on printed materials.

questions.q: What is another name for the Coercive Acts (1774)?
questions.explain: They were Britain's response to the Boston Tea Party.

questions.q: Who became Commander of the Continental Army?
questions.explain: Named by the Second Continental Congress.

questions.q: The Olive Branch Petition (July 1775) was…
choices: the colonists' last attempt at peace
questions.explain: It failed: George III issued a Proclamation of Rebellion on August 23, 1775.

questions.q: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July ___, 1776.
Which philosopher strongly influenced the Declaration of Independence?
questions.explain: It was influenced by the Enlightenment, especially John Locke.

questions.q: Which battle was the major American victory of 1781?
questions.explain: Supported by French troops, including Lafayette.

questions.q: Which treaty officially ended the Revolutionary War?
questions.explain: The 1763 Treaty of Paris ended the Seven Years' War.

questions.q: What is a confederation?
choices: A union of states with a weak central government
A strong central government above the states
questions.explain: A federation has a stronger central government.

questions.q: Under the Articles of Confederation, there was a president and a national judicial system.
questions.explain: No president, no national judicial system, no executive power, one chamber.

questions.q: Which figure is associated with the Federalists?
questions.explain: Federalists wanted a stronger central government.

questions.q: Shays' Rebellion (1786) showed…
questions.explain: It increased support for a new Constitution.

questions.q: The Virginia Plan proposed representation…
questions.explain: Large states supported it; small states preferred the New Jersey Plan.

questions.q: Under the Great Compromise, how many senators does each state have?
questions.explain: The House is proportional to population; the Senate is equal (2 per state).

questions.q: How many articles does the Constitution contain?
questions.explain: It begins with the Preamble 'We the People…'.

questions.q: Article II of the Constitution concerns…
questions.explain: I = legislative, II = executive, III = judicial.

questions.q: How many members does the House of Representatives have?
questions.explain: 100 senators, 435 representatives, 538 electors.

questions.q: How long is a senator's term?
questions.explain: Representatives serve 2-year terms.

questions.q: Since which amendment are senators directly elected?
questions.explain: Since 1913.

questions.q: How can Congress override a presidential veto?
questions.explain: A 2/3 majority in both the House and the Senate.

questions.q: What is a pocket veto?
choices: The President neither signs nor vetoes a bill as Congress ends its session
A veto by the Supreme Court
questions.explain: It happens when Congress is about to end its session.

questions.q: The Elastic Clause allows Congress to…
choices: make laws 'necessary and proper' to carry out its powers
questions.explain: Supported by loose constructionists, criticized by strict constructionists.

questions.q: How many electoral votes are needed to win the presidency?
questions.explain: There are 538 electors in total.

questions.q: How many electors does Washington, D.C. have?
questions.explain: Each state has House representatives + 2 senators; D.C. has 3.

questions.q: A candidate must win the national popular vote to become President.
On January 6, after a presidential election…
questions.explain: November: citizens vote. December: electors vote. January 6: Congress counts.

questions.q: In a midterm year…
choices: all House seats and about 1/3 of the Senate are elected
questions.explain: There is no presidential election in a midterm year.

questions.q: Which case established judicial review (1803)?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court can declare a law unconstitutional.

questions.q: In which year was Roe v. Wade overturned?
questions.explain: Abortion regulation returned largely to the states.

questions.q: How is an amendment adopted?
choices: 2/3 of both Houses, then 3/4 of the states
questions.explain: Article V makes it deliberately difficult.

questions.q: Which state was the ninth to ratify the Constitution (1788)?
questions.explain: 9 of the 13 states were needed (Article VII).

questions.q: What is the Bill of Rights?
questions.explain: It protects fundamental rights and liberties.

questions.q: Under the Three-Fifths Compromise, enslaved people were counted as…
choices: three-fifths of a person for representation
questions.explain: This gave Southern states more representatives without giving enslaved people rights.

questions.q: The importation of enslaved people could not be prohibited before ___.
questions.explain: Another compromise of the Constitution on slavery.

Put the steps of a bill in order
items: The bill is presented in the House
The President signs or vetoes it
